For the dye study, dye was injected at the inlet of Aerobic Z2, and samples were subsequently collected at the outlet of Aerobic Z3. Preliminary analysis suggested that the combined hydraulic behavior of Aerobic Z2 and Z3 could be approximated as a series of five CSTRs. To validate this assumption, a modelling study was performed. The model was created in Dynamita’s Sumo software and included five CSTRs equivalent in total volume to Aerobic Z2 and Z3. The modelling exercise consisted of a dynamic simulation in which a metal tracer was introduced in the influent of the first CSTR under flow conditions aligning with those from the day of the dye study. The mass of metal tracer injected in the model also matched the mass of dye introduced during the hands-on experiment. The results from this dye study and the modelling evaluation are displayed in Figure 5-15. The physical layout of the three zones upstream of the first common aerated channel comprises six CSTRs in-series. Altogether, it can be reasonably surmised that the biological 50 The Water Research Foundation process consists of 11 CSTRs in-series upstream of the NHx measurement taken at the Aerobic Z3 outlet (6 + 5 CSTRs for Aerobic Z2 & Z3). In addition to the predominantly plug flow hydraulic behavior, the influent NHx load entering Aerobic Z2 is characterized by significant variability. As illustrated in Figure 5-16, diurnal fluctuations in NHx concentration display inconsistent magnitudes and patterns. The presence or absence of a shoulder on the diurnal peak adds to this irregularity. Furthermore, extreme (rain) events, such as the pronounced peak depicted in the middle of the figure, exacerbate the unpredictable nature of the influent load. Åmand (2014), supported by operational experiences at the HRSD NTP, highlights the detrimental effects of locating the NHx measurement in the final aerated zone of similarly configured biological processes. These destabilizing delays hinder controller performance, as illustrated in Figure 5-17, displaying the performance of the baseline feedback-only ABAC controller and its inability to maintain Aerobic Z3 effluent NHx concentrations at setpoint. To address these shortcomings, the feedback approach can be expanded to include a feedforward component.
